title: The app never says whether a contract is Kept — Direction shows Draft/Locked only (surface.v1 Core 8, kit rule 8b)
description:
Measured with the retargeted surface kit against the running app (uv run conformance/surface/run.py http://127.0.0.1:8097 --changes-nothing '/direction/*/mark-read'):

  [FAIL] 8b  no contract is shown as Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check — the state beside each one is ['Draft'], which is the document's own status, not whether the promise is being kept

surface.v1 Core 8 fixes two vocabularies. The lane one is spoken: lane cards on Operation say Working / Quiet / Silent — may have died (kit rule 8a passes, 111 states shown, every one a plain word). The contract one is never spoken anywhere. src/amplifier_converge/words.py defines CONTRACT_STATES and maps the internal tokens onto them (conforms -> Kept, gap -> Not yet, violation -> Broken, open pinned -> Pinned open, ...), but nothing reads the ledger: `grep -rn "ledger\|rows.yaml\|CONFORMS" src` returns only words.py itself and the lane/queue/document readers, none of which touch ledger/rows.yaml.

So Direction shows five contracts each chipped `Draft` — the document's own status from its H1, which is documents.v1 clause 6, not surface.v1 clause 8. A steward opening Direction cannot see whether a promise is being kept, which is the whole of clause 8's first half.

ledger/rows.yaml is seeded (62 rows, each carrying a disposition), so the reading exists on disk; what is missing is a reader and a chip.

Owning path: src/amplifier_converge/reading/ (a ledger reader mapping each contract to its rows' worst disposition through words.surface_word) and src/amplifier_converge/web/pages.py (_document_row, to show it beside the Draft/Locked chip rather than instead of it).

Not fixed here: lane w5-surface-kit owns conformance/surface/** only; src/ is explicitly out of scope. The kit rule that catches this is new and stays FAIL until the app speaks the words.
acceptance: GIVEN the companion app reading a project whose ledger is seeded WHEN Direction is opened THEN each contract shows one of Kept · Not yet · Broken · Pinned open · Can't check against reality, alongside its own Draft/Locked status; AND `uv run conformance/surface/run.py <the running app>` reports rule 8b PASS.

title: Surface kit checks the mockup's markup, so the server-rendered app fails rules 1a–1e, 3a and 4
description:

  uv run conformance/surface/run.py <a page rendered by amplifier_converge.web>

— reports FAIL on 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e, 3a and 4 on every page, and PASS on 5.

The failures are not the app missing the promises. They are the kit looking for the *mockup's* way of keeping them: `data-goto` navigation, `#needCount`, `[data-answer]` controls, a `fillLanes` routine, a `#readiness` block, `#diffBtn`, `#filedList`, and script handlers wiring them together. The app keeps the same promises without any script at all — places are links to real routes, answering is a form POST that re-renders a shorter list, the lock control is a disabled button, what-changed is a rendered list of removed and added sentences, and every answer is written to the dated ratification record on disk. `tests/test_renders_at_both_widths.py::test_pages_are_server_rendered_with_no_script_at_all` asserts the app carries no script on purpose, so this is not something the app can satisfy by adding handlers.

Two rules also still SKIP with the reason "the app is not built yet (converge-2qh)", which is no longer true.

So a steward reading the kit's verdict on the app sees FAIL and cannot tell a real defect from a shape mismatch — which is exactly what a conformance kit exists to prevent.

Not attempted here: lane w3-app-vocab owns `src/amplifier_converge/**` only, and conformance/ is explicitly out of its scope.

Also open, from the same run: the verified mockup at /home/bkrabach/dev/vision-focused-team-ci/ai_working/converge-ux-mockups/index.html still FAILs rule 5 on "bundle" and "recipe" (four lines of card and lane copy, plus one promise sentence, named in converge-y7s). It lives in another repository, outside any file this lane may edit.
acceptance: GIVEN a page rendered by the companion app WHEN `uv run conformance/surface/run.py <page>` runs THEN each rule either PASSes, or FAILs for a reason that is a real defect in the app — never because the app keeps a promise a different way than the mockup did; AND no rule's SKIP reason says the app is not built yet.

title: Export the work queue to docs/work-items.json so documents rule 9a can run against this repo
description:

      and none named with --work-items — work items live in the work queue, not in

Rule 9a is mechanical and complete — it asserts both halves clause 9's first sentence names (an item names a contract that EXISTS in contracts/, by stem and version; and its definition of done carries no machine state word). It SKIPs here for one reason only: this repository exports no queue. That is a fixable absence, not a refusal, which is why CVG-051 is GAP and not NOT-ASSERTABLE.

The kit already accepts the export in two ways (conformance/documents/README.md, "Run it"): a JSON array or JSONL at `docs/work-items.json` in the target, found automatically, or an explicit `--work-items PATH`. Each object may carry `id`, `title`, `description`, `acceptance`, `design`, `notes`.

Known before starting: when converge-8om ran 9a against the live converge queue (24 items) it reported a real FAIL — 4 of 24 named no contract (converge-nht, converge-dxv, converge-l44, converge-5zk), filed as converge-vc0. So landing the export is expected to turn CVG-051 from GAP into a red row with a running check, which is progress, not a regression. Refreshing the export is also a policy question worth deciding in the same pass: a stale export would let rule 9a pass on a queue that has since changed.
acceptance: GIVEN this repository carries no work-item export, WHERE documents kit rule 9a SKIPs with "no work-item export at docs/work-items.json and none named with --work-items", WHEN an export of the converge work queue is committed at docs/work-items.json (JSON array or JSONL; objects carrying id, title, description, acceptance, design, notes), THEN `uv run conformance/documents/run.py .` reports rule 9a with status PASS or FAIL rather than SKIP, and its reason names the item count it read. title: lane-brief genre: an evidence-printing criterion must state the falsity condition, not only the presence condition
description:
Serves documents.v1. Ruled a brief defect (not a lane defect) by converge:protocol-authority, 2026-09-03, on review of lane w4-doc-kit-2's close.

WHAT THE BRIEF SAID

Lane w4-doc-kit-2's acceptance criterion 4 read, verbatim:

  "4. Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back."

WHAT HAPPENED

Both items were resolved and both reasons were printed — so the criterion was met exactly as written. But one of the two stored reasons contained a false paragraph, and the tracker will not let a resolution be corrected once an item closes (filed as work_tracker item work_item_pipeline-03c). The lane superseded the record and disclosed the defect, and the criterion still read PASS.

That produced a genuine, repeated disagreement about whether the lane had met its goal: the criterion's literal text was satisfied while its evident purpose — trustworthy evidence — was not. Under PROTOCOL.md section 7 the literal reading governs, because re-reading a briefed criterion at grading time to mean something stricter is a self-ratified amendment of the brief, which is forbidden to lanes and to the orchestrator alike. So the lane closed as SUCCESS-with-residual, correctly, and the ambiguity survived.

THE DEFECT

PROTOCOL.md section 4 requires a lane brief to carry an honesty gate: name what "not proven" looks like before work starts. Criterion 4 named what ABSENT evidence looks like — a reason not printed — and never named what FALSE evidence looks like. That omission is why the two readings could diverge at all.

THE CHANGE

The lane-brief genre should require that any criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself authors states both conditions:

  - the presence condition: the artifact exists and is shown
  - the falsity condition: what makes the shown artifact unsound, and what the lane must do if it discovers its own artifact is wrong after it is written

Criterion 4 would then have read something closer to: "Both items resolved; each stored reason printed via work_list read-back; if a printed reason is found to be false, the correction must be reachable from the reason itself, not only from a linked item."

Applies to future briefs. It does not regrade w4-doc-kit-2, which finished against the version it was briefed on (PROTOCOL.md section 5).

The skill to change is skills/lane-brief.
acceptance: GIVEN the lane-brief skill WHEN an author writes a criterion whose evidence is an artifact the lane itself produces THEN the skill requires them to state what makes that artifact unsound, alongside what makes it present; AND it says what a lane must do when it finds its own evidence wrong after writing it; AND a worked example shows a criterion written both ways, so an author can see which one survives a lane that made a mistake and caught it.

title: candidate-guard does not honor the new proposal name <contract>.vN-candidate.md
description:

  - line 101: candidate_glob      default = ["**/CANDIDATE-*.md"]

modules/ is outside W1's file ownership (skills/** and agents/** content only), so this was not fixed in-lane.

THEN the escape hatch finds the ratified proposal under the new name and allows the edit
AND the denial message names `<contract>.vN-candidate.md` as the form to write.

title: Guard does not cover `amplifier tool invoke` — direct CLI dispatch bypasses tool:pre
description:

In a scratch repo holding a FROZEN `contracts/probe.v1.md`, running

(8 bytes). The same module's `evaluate_tool_pre()`, called directly on the
byte-identical input against the same fixture, returns action="deny".

appears to run outside the `tool:pre` hook pipeline the guard registers on.
This weakens composition.v1 clause 7 ("refuses every other write to a locked
contract, by person or agent") on that path.

Not fixed here: the hook module owns no wiring, and the cause is plausibly an
upstream app-CLI property (hooks are session-scoped) rather than a bundle
defect. Documented as non-coverage in modules/hooks-candidate-guard/README.md
"Known gaps".

Note for whoever picks this up: the shared `converge` bundle registration
points at a concurrent lane's worktree and flipped from present to absent
mid-session, so re-probing needs its own stable registration.

title: Documents: contract clause 4 is silent on whether a contract may carry an EXTRA section
description:
Surfaced while building the documents.v1 conformance kit — an interpretive gap the kit refused to decide on the steward's behalf.

documents.v1 Core 4 says: "The same sections, in the same order, every time. Purpose -> Core (the teeth) -> What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze (with promotion triggers) -> Conformance kit asserts -> Reserved / open questions -> Changelog only if amended."

It fixes PRESENCE and ORDER. It does not say whether a SEVENTH section is permitted.

contracts/operation.v1.md carries one: "## Declared dependencies (checked at install)", between Core and "What v1 deliberately does NOT freeze".

Two readings, both defensible:
  (a) "the same sections ... every time" fixes the SET — an extra section is a violation, and operation.v1 should fold that content into an existing section.
  (b) The clause fixes order and required presence only — an extra section is fine, and the kit should stay quiet.

The kit implements neither ruling. Rule 1b asserts only what the contract unambiguously fixes (presence and order) and REPORTS any extra section in the row's detail, so the fact is visible without inventing a rule:

  contracts/operation.v1.md -> all five required sections, in order
    (also carries: ['Declared dependencies (checked at install)'])

Deciding this is a documents.v1 amendment (a clarifying sentence in clause 4), not a code change. If reading (a) wins, rule 1b tightens to fail an extra section and operation.v1 needs an edit; if (b) wins, clause 4 should say so explicitly so the next reader does not re-derive this question.

Reproduce:
  uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only | python3 -c "import json,sys;[print(f['file'],'->',f['detail']) for x in json.load(sys.stdin)['results'] if x['rule']=='1b' for f in x['files']]"
acceptance: GIVEN documents.v1 clause 4 WHEN a reader asks "may a contract carry a section beyond the six listed?" THEN the clause answers it in one sentence — and if the answer is no, conformance/documents rule 1b fails an extra section and contracts/operation.v1.md no longer carries one.

title: Documents: six kit rules assert less than their clause text says (ledger rows CVG-058/059/061/063/064/065)
description:

title: Split CVG-051 — clause 9's two halves no longer share a disposition after wave 4
description:
Serves documents.v1 Core 9. Found while working converge-12o, which owned the four red rows (CVG-052/053/057/066) and the stale `indexed` refs, and deliberately did not guess at this fifth re-derivation.

CVG-051 is one GAP row quoting the whole of clause 9: "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words, and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." Before wave 4 that was right — rule 4 SKIPped because "work items live in the work queue, not in the repository", and nothing asserted any part of the clause.

Wave 4 replaced that with two rules, and they are no longer the same kind of thing (RAN 2026-09-03, `uv run conformance/documents/run.py . --json-only`):

  9a  work_item_names_a_contract   SKIP  "no work-item export at docs/work-items.json
      and none named with --work-items — work items live in the work queue, not in
      this tree, so the kit has nothing to read"
  9b  work_item_quotes_its_source  SKIP  "measured against this repository's own
      queue: the literal test — a blockquote or a quoted span — passes 7 of 24 real
      items, and most of the 17 it fails do point at their origin … Telling a
      quotation of feedback from a quoted filename needs a reader."

9a is a plain GAP: the check exists, it is mechanical, and it SKIPs only because this repository exports no queue. Supply `docs/work-items.json` (or `--work-items`) and it runs. 9b is a MEASURED refusal — the same shape as rule 7d, which is exactly why converge-jc9 moved CVG-063 to NOT-ASSERTABLE rather than leaving it GAP.

A row whose two halves carry different dispositions is one this ledger splits, quoting a disjoint sentence for each (CVG-059 → CVG-067 in wave 4; CVG-052 → CVG-068 in converge-12o). The likely shape: CVG-051 keeps "**A work item names its contract** in one line, defines done in plain words," as GAP against rule 9a, and a new id takes "and quotes the feedback or gap it came from." as NOT-ASSERTABLE against rule 9b's measurement.

Worth deciding in the same pass: whether exporting the work queue to docs/work-items.json is work this repo wants, since that alone would let 9a actually run and could move the GAP half.

converge-12o updated CVG-051's `indexed` ref from the stale `(rule 4)` — which after the renumber names `contract_section_order` under Core 4 — to `(rules 9a, 9b)`, and re-derived its notes against the run above. The disposition was left at GAP, which under-claims rather than over-claims, and is honest for the row as it currently stands.
acceptance: GIVEN the documents kit as merged at wave 4, WHERE rule 9a SKIPs for a missing export and rule 9b SKIPs on a measurement, WHEN CVG-051 is split so each half quotes its own disjoint sentence of clause 9 and carries the disposition its own rule supports, THEN `uv run --with pyyaml ledger/checks/verify.py` prints and exits 0 with clause 9 still cited, each new row carries a RAN line naming the rule and verdict it was derived from, and the NOT-ASSERTABLE half carries a justification quoting rule 9b's own measured reason. Falsified by: a disposition assigned without a run shown, overlapping quotes between the two halves, or a `work` ref left on a row that is no longer red.

title: Corrected record for converge-nht — its stored resolution contains a retracted false claim that cannot be edited
description:
Serves documents.v1. This item exists to carry a TRUE resolution for work that is finished, because the resolution stored on converge-nht is false and the tracker will not let it be corrected.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH converge-nht's STORED RESOLUTION

It states: "This repository has no ledger — there is no ledger/ directory and no rows.yaml at any commit, and AGENTS.md §3 still says the ledger does not exist yet."

That is false. ledger/rows.yaml is on main (seeded 3c7fdfb; revised c1a4005, bd61d86, d96c379) and on lane/w4-wiring. Lane w4-doc-kit-2 branched at 8b54020, eighteen commits before it landed, so the file is absent from that worktree only. The lane ran `git log -- ledger` against one branch, got nothing, and reported on the repository. `git log --all -- ledger` returns four commits.

It also describes the work as covering "documents.v1 Core 5, 9, 10 and 11". Those are the clauses converge-nht's DESCRIPTION named. The six ledger rows its TITLE and ACCEPTANCE name are Core 1, 2, 6, 7, 12 and 13. The item contradicts itself and the resolution followed the wrong half.

WHY IT CANNOT BE FIXED IN PLACE — both paths tried, both refused

  work_claim(converge-nht)  -> "claim failed: issue not claimable: status closed"
  amplifier-work-tracker resolve --id converge-nht --reason <corrected>
                            -> exit 0, and echoed back the ORIGINAL resolution
                               unchanged (a readback-checked no-op, as the CLI's
                               own help documents)

work_edit / `edit` can rewrite title, description, acceptance and design — every field except the one that is wrong. So the retraction lives on converge-nht's description, in a different field from the claim it retracts, and this item carries the corrected reason in a resolution field where a reader looking at resolutions will actually find it.

Nothing further is to be BUILT here. The work is committed on lane/w4-doc-kit-2 (5fe18cd, acc77b8, ca4036f) and the kit is green. Resolve this item with the corrected reason and read it back; that read-back is the honest evidence converge-nht's own resolution can no longer provide.

The remaining real work — moving the six ledger rows off GAP — is converge-jc9, not this.
acceptance: GIVEN converge-nht's stored resolution, which cannot be edited, WHEN this item is resolved and read back THEN its stored reason states what the lane actually did, names the six ledger rows by the clauses they really cover, and retracts the false claim about the ledger in the field a reader checks; AND the link from this item to converge-nht makes the replacement findable from either end.
